text: Money is both. <break time="0.8s" /> A tool to help us create working relationships with strangers. <break time="0.8s" /> And a mirror that reflects our values and fears. <break time="0.8s" /> Modern people are far more isolated. <break time="0.8s" /> Than our ancestors. <break time="0.8s" /> When our ancestors created money. <break time="0.8s" /> They were worried about security. <break time="0.8s" /> Rather than intimacy. <break time="0.8s" /> They used money. <break time="0.8s" /> To widen their connections with people outside their intimate circles. <break time="0.8s" /> This allowed them. <break time="0.8s" /> To create working relationships. <break time="0.8s" /> Which in turn helped them. <break time="0.8s" /> Increase their sense of stability in their lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Within their close knit groups. <break time="0.8s" /> They did not need money. <break time="0.8s" /> To clarify or maintain their relationships. <break time="0.8s" /> For the most part they could trust. <break time="0.8s" /> That the people in their lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Would be there when needed. <break time="0.8s" /> Our ancestors could take their sense of belonging for granted. <break time="0.8s" /> As they rarely traveled. <break time="0.8s" /> Beyond the boundaries of their communities. <break time="0.8s" /> A person living within relatively constrained borders. <break time="0.8s" /> Generally has a clear role and sense of purpose. <break time="0.8s" /> Within their tribe.
